official_sources: Compulsory purchase and compensation guide 1 procedure
Town and Country Planning Act 1990 section 226

official_measurement_examples.name: June 2026 CPO guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: National compulsory-purchase guidance was updated 17 June 2026 and sets out separate stages from choosing powers through confirmation, implementation and compensation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Decision register currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: The national housing, planning and regeneration CPO decision register was updated 28 April 2026; a register entry records a decision and must retain decision date and order status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Made order versus confirmed order
official_measurement_examples.fact: An acquiring authority making a CPO does not by itself complete acquisition; confirmation or another statutory outcome and later implementation steps remain separate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Confirmation versus possession
official_measurement_examples.fact: Confirmation of a CPO authorises the compulsory-purchase process but is not proof that title has already transferred or possession has been taken.

official_measurement_examples.name: Purchase notice limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A purchase notice does not automatically require a council to buy land unless it accepts the notice, it is confirmed, or another statutory confirmation route applies.

official_measurement_examples.name: Hope-value direction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A section 14A direction removing hope value is available only in specified circumstances and must be justified in the public interest; it is not a universal compensation rule for every CPO.

official_measurement_examples.name: Crichel Down distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Crichel Down Rules are non-statutory arrangements about offering certain surplus compulsorily acquired government land back; they do not undo the original acquisition automatically.

official_measurement_examples.name: CPO versus planning permission
official_measurement_examples.fact: A compulsory-purchase power, order or compensation process is distinct from planning permission and does not itself establish development capacity for the acquired land.

core_rules: made CPO is not confirmed CPO
confirmed CPO is not completed title transfer
CPO confirmation is distinct from possession
compensation assessment is distinct from planning permission
purchase notice is not automatic council acquisition
hope-value direction is case-specific and power-specific
Crichel Down Rules are non-statutory disposal arrangements
decision register entry retains date and order status
CPO boundary is not proof of current registered title after implementation changes
historic CPO geometry must retain version and operative status
objection or inquiry stage is not confirmation outcome
acquisition power does not calculate parcel development yield
planning permission does not itself complete compulsory acquisition
absence from one decision register is not proof no other acquiring-power process exists
no Future Growth promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. June 2026 CPO guidance and April 2026 decision register were preserved with order, confirmation, possession, title and compensation-stage separation; no parcel promotion.
